Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Samir Gupta (Redwood SE), Maya Lopez (StratoDynamics HO ML), Derek Shaw (DevOps), Priya Singh (CTO)

Summary:
Quick discovery focused on migration from OpenAI hosted usage to Redwood Dedicated - compatibility concerns (vLLM/TGI), eval parity, cost/latency tradeoffs, and security/compliance requirements for regulated telemetry. Agreed to run pilot benchmarks and exchange security docs.

Topics:
- Current stack and pain points
- Performance and eval parity vs OpenAI (quality, latency)
- vLLM/TGI compatibility and open-source runtime differences
- Networking, VPC, data residency, KMS
- Pricing and dedicated capacity sizing

Transcript:
[00:00] Laura Chen: Hi everyone, thanks for joining - Laura from Redwood, i'm the AE on this - with Samir our SE. How are you all?
[00:05] Maya Lopez: Hey Laura, good thanks. We have limited time so want to get straight into our migration story.
[00:09] Derek Shaw: Yep, appreciate it. We currently run most inference with OpenAI via API, and some experimental runs on vLLM for on-prem proofs.
[00:14] Laura Chen: Got it, great. Can you share high level goals for moving off OpenAI to a dedicated/private setup?
[00:20] Priya Singh: Primarily predictable cost and higher throughput, plus we need more control for data residency and audit requirements. Also want to avoid regressions in answer quality - eval parity is big.
[00:28] Samir Gupta: Cool - when you say eval parity, do you have an existing eval harness and baseline numbers?
[00:33] Maya Lopez: We do, it's a mix of unit prompts and customer conversations. We run bench scripts against OpenAI and compare Rouge/BLEU-ish metrics and also human judgment on a subset.
[00:41] Derek Shaw: The issue is latency spikes during peak business hours; costs balloon. We looked at vLLM on k8s but couldn't get consistent tail latencies.
[00:49] Laura Chen: That sounds familiar. Our Dedicated offering gives reserved GPU pools with autoscale and predictable throughput; we also expose batching and KV cache controls to tune cost vs latency.
[00:58] Maya Lopez: Two questions: 1) Will our prompts behave identically on Redwood to OpenAI? and 2) what about the model variants - we use GPT-4-ish family from OpenAI now.
[01:08] Samir Gupta: On compatibility: Redwood serves model artifacts (open checkpoints) and also provides Redwood-verified performance profiles. If you're using OpenAI proprietary models, you'd need to pick a compatible open model we recommend, or run privately hosted replicas. We do model mapping exercises to find parity candidates; sometimes that involves small prompt adjustments.
[01:23] Priya Singh: Right, we were worried about subtle output drift. We can't afford a degradation in downstream metrics.
[01:28] Laura Chen: Totally - that's why we run eval parity work during the pilot. We take your eval set, run on a few candidate models (and quantization profiles) and show side-by-side results: latency, token cost, and quality metrics. Often small prompt tweaks recover parity.
[01:39] Derek Shaw: Can you run our existing scripts? they're in a private bitbucket repo. We can't share the raw data externally.
[01:45] Samir Gupta: Yes, we can run benchmarks in Dedicated or a Private deployment. For security we can sign an NDA; for early pilots we typically run on a isolated Redwood Dedicated pod or on your VPC with telemetry redacted.
[01:55] Maya Lopez: Also, our infra team uses TGI and vLLM for internal tests. We're concerned about runtime differences - e.g., vLLM KV cache handling and memory behaviour when quantized.
[02:04] Samir Gupta: Good point. vLLM and TGI are inference runtimes; Redwood's runtime includes kernel selection and cache management optimized for GPU backends. We do support running model weights with quantized profiles and our runtime handles KV cache to keep latency predictable. Sometimes vLLM configs that work locally need different batching settings in a multi-tenant or dedicated environment.
[02:20] Priya Singh: So basically you take care of the heavy infra tuning and we get a consistent SLO.
[02:23] Laura Chen: Exactly - and when you'd like total control, our Private deployment gives you the control plane in your VPC or on-prem; Dedicated is a reserved pool in our environment but isolated to your account.
[02:33] Derek Shaw: Networking question: egress and IP allowlists - we have strict firewall rules; can Redwood fit behind our NAT and allowlist?
[02:39] Samir Gupta: Yes, we support customer-managed networking for Private deployments. For Dedicated we have peering options and static egress ranges, and we can coordinate with your security team. We'll need your network topology to size routes and ensure low-latency paths to GPUs.
[02:52] Maya Lopez: Compliance: we need SOC2, ISO, and key management with our KMS (HashiCorp Vault).
[02:57] Laura Chen: We have SOC2 and ISO docs; we also support KMS integrations and HSM for Private. I'll attach SOC2 doc and our security whitepaper.
[03:06] Priya Singh: Great - costs: what is difference in unit economics between Hosted API and Dedicated? We saw rough numbers but need concrete estimates for our workload.
[03:15] Laura Chen: We'll send a dedicated pricing sheet with committed capacity tiers; rough rule of thumb is Dedicated offers 30 - 60% savings at scale depending on batching and caching, but we need your request profile to give precise numbers.
[03:26] Derek Shaw: For the pilot, what hardware do you recommend? our prompts average 600 tokens and we use context windows up to 4k.
[03:34] Samir Gupta: For 4k context and 600 average with high throughput, a mix of A100 or H100 class GPUs depending on model selection; we'll propose GPU counts in the sizing doc. For quantized models you can often use more cost-effective GPUs.
[03:45] Maya Lopez: We also run embeddings at large scale for semantic search - will that be on same cluster or separate?
[03:50] Laura Chen: You can isolate embeddings on a separate pool - Redwood routing lets you split by route/model, so embeddings can be sent to an optimized pool. That helps cost control.
[03:58] Priya Singh: About model weights - do you host our custom fine-tuned weights? or do we need to bring them?
[04:03] Samir Gupta: We support customer-provided model artifacts, including private weights. For Private deployments you retain full control. For Dedicated we can host them under strict access controls and audit logs.
[04:12] Derek Shaw: Any cloud vendor lock-in? We currently use Azure primarily.
[04:16] Laura Chen: Redwood has multi-region support; Dedicated can be deployed on cloud infra we operate or on your cloud via Private. We avoid lock-in on the model side - you get model artifacts and the option to export configs.
[04:25] Maya Lopez: One more technical: we've noticed vLLM sometimes OOMs on long sequences when the kv cache is warm. How does Redwood mitigate that?
[04:32] Samir Gupta: Our runtime manages KV cache and memory allocation; we also provide quantization recommendations and per-request memory budgeting. Part of the pilot is to reproduce those failure modes and tune batching / cache eviction to avoid OOMs.
[04:42] Priya Singh: Sounds promising. Let's talk timeline - we want a 6 - 8 week pilot that runs our eval suite and a small production migration plan after.
[04:49] Laura Chen: That's doable. Typical flow: 1) security paperwork + NDA, 2) pilot provisioning (dedicated or private), 3) run parity benchmarks, 4) iterate on prompts and quantization, 5) production rollout. We'll work with your timelines.
[04:60] Derek Shaw: Quick note, that's 04:60 but i meant 05:00.
[05:00] Maya Lopez: Ha - timings are fuzzy.
[05:02] Laura Chen: Action recap: I'll share SOC2/ISO and pricing; Samir will prepare a benchmark runbook and candidate model mapping; Derek will share topology and the eval corpus. We'll plan a technical deep dive next Tuesday.
[05:14] Priya Singh: Ok agree. Any blockers for us to start?
[05:17] Samir Gupta: The main blocker is access to your eval set and network requirements; otherwise we can spin up a pilot environment quickly.
[05:23] Laura Chen: Cool - we'll follow up with calendar invites and docs. Thanks everyone.
[05:27] Maya Lopez: Thanks Laura, Samir.
[05:28] Derek Shaw: Thanks.
[05:29] Priya Singh: Thank you.
